public class Login extends androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
Login is the profile management screen for authenticated users of the app.

After a successful login, the user's full profile data is passed into this activity via an intent extra. The profile is parsed and displayed immediately, no second network request is needed. Users can then update their bio directly from this screen using the Save Profile button, which sends a PUT request to the backend with the updated data.

The activity receives everything it needs from LoginActivity and only makes a network call when the user explicitly chooses to save changes. This keeps the experience fast and avoids unnecessary data usage.

Edit endpoint: PUT /users/{id}

  • Method Details

    • onCreate

      protected void onCreate(android.os.Bundle savedInstanceState)
      Called when the activity is first created.

      Sets up the profile screen by reading the user ID and full user JSON from the incoming intent. If a valid JSON string is present, it is parsed into a User object using parseUserFromJson(JSONObject) and the UI is populated immediately. The name and bio fields are pre-filled with the user's existing data so they can edit only what they want to change.

      The Save Profile button is disabled by default and only becomes enabled once the profile has been loaded successfully. This prevents accidental empty submissions before the data has arrived.

      Overrides:
      onCreate in class androidx.fragment.app.FragmentActivity
      Parameters:
      savedInstanceState - Bundle containing the activity's previously saved state, or null if this is a fresh launch.

    • parseUserFromJson

      public User parseUserFromJson(org.json.JSONObject response) throws org.json.JSONException
      Parses a JSON object returned by the server into a User model object.

      This method handles inconsistencies between different field name conventions that may come from the backend. for example, user_id vs userId, name vs displayName, createdAt vs createdTs, and isActive vs active. This defensive parsing ensures the app works reliably even if the backend changes its field naming convention.

      If the parsed user ID comes back as zero (which can happen with certain JSON structures), it falls back to parsing the ID as a string. This covers edge cases where the server returns the ID as a string value rather than a numeric one.

      Hobbies are parsed from a JSON array if present. If the field is missing or null, an empty list is used instead so the rest of the app never has to deal with a null hobbies field.

      Parameters:
      response - The JSON object from the server containing user data.
      Returns:
      A fully populated User object, or throws if parsing fails critically.
      Throws:
      org.json.JSONException - If a required field cannot be read from the JSON object.

    • updateUserProfile

      public void updateUserProfile()
      Sends a PUT request to update the currently logged-in user's profile on the server.

      Reads the updated bio from the input field and constructs a JSON request body. The user's age is also included in the body if it is a valid positive value, since the backend expects it to be present alongside the bio for the edit endpoint.

      On a successful response, the local User object is updated with the new bio value and the UI is refreshed immediately so the change is reflected on screen without needing to reload the page. A success toast confirms the update to the user.

      On failure, an error toast is shown and the issue is logged for debugging. The local user object is left unchanged in this case.

      Endpoint: PUT /users/{id}

    • refreshUI

      public void refreshUI()
      Rebuilds and updates the profile display TextView with the latest user data.

      Called both when the profile is first loaded and after a successful update. Formats the user's name, email, bio, major, age, creation timestamp, and active status into a readable multi-line string. Hobbies and role are appended at the end only if they are present and non-empty, keeping the display clean for users who haven't filled in those fields.
